newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese t-bill rates to fall further-bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese t-bill rates to fall further-bank chief.

text.p: Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh on Tuesday forecast an accelerated fall in Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bill rates.
However, he said the fall in rates would be for the time being relative rather than fundamental, indicating that the level of the decline would be limited.

"The continuing retreat in Lebanese pound treasury bill rates and the movement of most subscriptions to two-year bills indicate a bigger retreat in the rates without threatening the local currency's exchange rate," Salameh told Arab bankers at a conference in Beirut.
"This retreat will be relative and will not become fundamental except after improving the productivity of the Lebanese economy by increasing imports and cutting the budget deficit," he added.
The Bank of Lebanon has recently reduced rates for its weekly t-bill issues at a slightly faster rate than it has in the past few months.
Yields currently stand at 14.43 percent for three-month bills while six month bills yield 16.67 percent, one-year bills 17.57 percent and two-year bills 21.26 percent.
